newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr closes flat in quiet pre-holiday trades.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr closes flat in quiet pre-holiday trades.

text.p: * Canada's dollar closed slightly softer at C$1.3667 (US$0.7317) from Wednesday's close of C$1.3659 (US$0.7322) after trading in a tight range all day Thursday.
* Market players were waiting for Friday's release of second quarter GDP and current account data, dealers said.
* Dealers expected activity to pick up Tuesday.
"It's the end of summer. Everything will get into swing next Tuesday," said another dealer.
But the market was keeping an eye out for second quarter GDP and current account data expected Friday, he said.
The market is expecting a current account surplus, but if the numbers don't live up to expectations, the market could move, he explained.
A Reuter survey of economists forecast a current account surplus of about C$500 million. It would be the first surplus in 12 years.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar weakened to 1.0801 marks from Wednesday's close at 1.0814 marks and to 79.24 yen from 79.37 yen.
